stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after resignation
stories.dek: The board voted unanimously after input from senior US officials, Trump says Huang "did nothing wrong," and staff cheered his return at headquarters.
stories.body:
Nvidia's board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, 11 days after he resigned amid reports of multiple affairs. The company said the move was effective immediately and followed meetings in which the board became "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA."

The board also said it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Appearing on CNBC, President Trump said he had spoken to the board "directly and indirectly" and that Huang "did nothing wrong," Ars Technica reports. Trump had publicly urged the rehiring on Truth Social last week. Tom's Hardware reports that Huang returns as president, CEO and board member, with Harvey C. Jones remaining chair. Ars Technica describes him as reinstated as board chair as well.

Investors cheered. Shares jumped more than 30 percent before the Nasdaq opened, erasing losses from Huang's absence, according to Tom's Hardware, which later put the gain at more than 32 percent. The stock had fallen 24 percent during his 11-day exit.

The controversy is far from over. Huang admitted an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US intelligence sources believe was working for Chinese intelligence, Ars Technica reports. Megaspeed is under criminal investigation over illicit exports of AI GPUs to China. A second affair, with Nvidia VP of health care Kimberly Powell, prompted his resignation. Huang still faces a board investigation, an SEC probe and congressional inquiries. Nvidia has formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors and is hiring a Chief Compliance Officer.

At headquarters, videos showed employees on multiple floors applauding Huang, who wore a wool fleece instead of his usual leather jacket. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reported that Huang called it his "first day of work" and promised, "I am gonna be a better CEO the second time around." Not everyone agreed. An anonymous engineer told Yahoo Finance: "This is the worst outcome."

CFO Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, keeps her finance role.
key_points: Nvidia board unanimously reinstated Huang 11 days after he resigned
Board cited input from senior US government officials on security risk
Shares rose more than 30 percent after the announcement
Board, SEC and congressional investigations continue
stories.why_it_matters: The man steering GeForce and the AI chip market is back, but open probes into export controls and China ties could still shape Nvidia's products and policy.

cover.caption: Nvidia stock gain since Huang's reinstatement, per Tom's Hardware

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn

stories.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX to stop Grok's sexual deepfakes
stories.dek: The first state lawsuits say Grok still sexualizes real photos of women and children, and call the company's safety promises misleading.
stories.body:
Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX on Monday, becoming the first states to take the company to court over Grok, the AI model it inherited when it acquired xAI in February. The attorneys general allege that Grok continues to sexualize real photos, mostly of women and children, without meaningful checks, according to Ars Technica.

The suits target the fallout from Grok's "spicy mode," a feature Elon Musk promoted. Ars Technica reports it was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material. Early safeguards were so weak that Grok sometimes produced nude images without being asked.

X Safety and xAI, now known as SpaceXSI, were initially silent. Musk's companies later apologized and said they had added safeguards and redesigned policies to block harmful outputs. The states call those statements "misleading." They allege that SpaceXSI instead quietly "embraced" sexualized content to win more of the AI market, and that Grok still generates such images today.

The complaints stress that the damage is hard to undo. "Once created and shared," such images "can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child's abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child's life," Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones' complaint said. "Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm."

The states say millions of residents were harmed, and they are seeking to protect every Grok and X user within their borders. They allege victims are likely to suffer chronic anxiety, depression and PTSD, along with reputational harm, since some viewers may not realize the images are AI-generated. Because Grok is built into X, the states also argue that users as young as 13 may have been exposed to the content and could be re-traumatized if they are themselves survivors of sexual abuse.

The cases put the AI unit of Musk's rocket company in a direct legal fight with state law enforcement. Whether other states join the effort is not yet known.
key_points: Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue SpaceX over Grok
States allege Grok still generates CSAM and non-consensual intimate images
Company safety claims called misleading by the attorneys general
Users as young as 13 may have been exposed via X, states say
stories.why_it_matters: State attorneys general are testing whether AI makers can be held liable when image models produce abusive content despite public safety promises. The outcome could shape how much guardrail work any shipped image-generation feature legally requires.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials

stories.headline: Azure API Management flaw exploited to steal stored credentials
stories.dek: Microsoft says its fix does not invalidate secrets already taken, and Norway links the bug to attacks on energy firms including Equinor.
stories.body:
Microsoft is warning customers that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, BleepingComputer reports. Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) links the flaw to cyberattacks on the country's energy sector.

In a Service Health advisory, Microsoft said it identified the issue on November 18 and deployed a mitigation the next day. The bug allowed unauthorized access to management functionality on APIM Classic instances not configured to recommended best practices, letting attackers perform administrative operations. Affected tiers are Developer, Basic, Standard and Premium. The Consumption tier and all APIM v2 tiers were not affected, the company says.

Exposed data may include secrets in Named Values, client secrets for identity and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys and tokens for direct management APIs. Microsoft closed the access path on November 19 and rotated keys it controls, but warned the fix "does not automatically invalidate credentials that may have been accessed before the fix was deployed." It urges customers to rotate exposed credentials, investigate suspicious activity and review logs.

NSM says an unknown threat actor targeted tokens, secrets and named values, that Norway's energy sector first discovered the flaw, and that organizations in other countries and industries were also hit. Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on November 17, a day before Microsoft says it found the bug, and later said it had stopped the attack with no sign of data theft or alteration. Skagerak Energi reported an attempted attack with no operational impact.

The guidance diverges on one point. Microsoft says its remediation was fully deployed to Microsoft-hosted instances and required no customer action. NSM advises organizations to verify their runtime versions, warning that instances below certain versions remain vulnerable. Microsoft did not explain the discrepancy.

An administrator on Reddit claimed attackers used a zero-day authentication bypass in a deprecated legacy API that produced no customer-visible logs, and that Microsoft first blamed leaked customer credentials. BleepingComputer has not verified those claims. The incident follows a separate Entra Connect Health breach Microsoft confirmed days earlier.
key_points: Flaw hit APIM Classic Developer, Basic, Standard and Premium tiers
Microsoft fixed it November 19 but stolen secrets stay valid until rotated
Norway's NSM ties it to attacks on Equinor and Skagerak Energi
NSM says some runtime versions remain vulnerable; Microsoft says no action needed
stories.why_it_matters: Teams running APIM Classic should rotate every secret, key and token stored in it now, since Microsoft's patch does not revoke anything already stolen. Check runtime versions too, given NSM's warning.

cover.caption: APIM Classic tiers hit by the exploited flaw

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: Ladybird is now in alpha

stories.headline: Ladybird browser reaches alpha with its own from-scratch engine
stories.dek: The independent browser is now downloadable for macOS and Linux, with automatic rolling updates and an open invitation to hackers.
stories.body:
Ladybird, the independent browser built on its own engine, is now in alpha. Builds are available for macOS and Linux, according to a post on the project's site. The announcement topped Hacker News with more than 1,600 points and 384 comments.

The engine was built from the ground up and is not a fork of an existing one. The project calls the browser around it "modest, but functional" and warns that some sites won't work and that crashes will happen. Users can report broken sites from inside the browser and choose whether to send crash reports. The team makes no security promises yet and asks researchers to report any successful attacks.

The alpha is a rolling channel with regular automatic updates. Until now, trying Ladybird meant building it from source. Web developers can test their sites using WebDriver and the Firefox DevTools protocol.
key_points: Ladybird's alpha is available for macOS and Linux as a rolling channel with automatic updates.
The browser uses its own engine built from scratch, not a fork.
The project makes no security promises yet and supports WebDriver and the Firefox DevTools protocol for testing.

sources.title: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer

stories.headline: Z.ai unveils GLM-5.4, its first loop transformer model
stories.dek: The lab pitches GLM-5.4 as a step toward generalized coding, and the announcement drew more than 1,000 points on Hacker News.
stories.body:
Z.ai has announced GLM-5.4, a new model in its GLM line that the lab describes as its first loop transformer. The company frames the release as a move "toward generalized coding," according to the title of its blog post published November 23.

The announcement quickly drew attention from developers. On Hacker News, it collected 1,094 points and 357 comments.

Loop transformers are an architecture explored in research in which the same layers are applied repeatedly rather than stacked once. Z.ai has not been quoted on how GLM-5.4 implements the approach, how it performs on coding benchmarks or when and how it will be available.
key_points: Z.ai calls GLM-5.4 its first loop transformer model.
The lab bills the release as a step toward generalized coding.
The announcement reached 1,094 points and 357 comments on Hacker News.

sources.name: Insurance Journal (Bloomberg)
sources.title: OpenAI chief scientist Pachocki proposes industry-wide limits on AI development

stories.headline: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes industry-wide limits on AI
stories.dek: Jakub Pachocki wants labs to agree not to cross capability thresholds, partly measured by perplexity, until AI monitoring reaches set milestones.
stories.body:
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that AI companies agree to common limits on developing more powerful models until researchers can better understand and monitor their behavior, Bloomberg reports. In a post published Sunday, he called for limits "based on perplexity and other measurements" that developers would not cross until oversight reaches "a certain concrete milestone." Perplexity gauges how well a model predicts the next piece of text. Pachocki did not say what the first limit should be or when it would take effect.

He warned that AI could speed up its own development as soon as 2027, possibly outpacing progress in monitoring. CEO Sam Altman called the essay "the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile."

The proposal lands as Democrats, fresh from sweeping midterm gains, prepare to push AI safety rules. President Donald Trump opposes broad restrictions.
key_points: Pachocki proposes shared limits, partly based on perplexity, that labs would not exceed until AI monitoring hits concrete milestones.
He warns AI could accelerate its own development as soon as 2027; no initial limit or timeline was given.
Sam Altman endorsed the essay, saying common limits would help ensure "safety and control."

sources.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning

stories.headline: Attackers exploit ScreenConnect flaw to hijack MSP technician PCs
stories.dek: A guest in a remote session can push and run a payload on the technician's machine with no prompt, Huntress says.
stories.body:
Attackers are exploiting a now-patched critical flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to take over the workstations of managed service provider (MSP) technicians, according to security firm Huntress. The bug, CVE-2026-84869, carries a CVSS score of 9.9. It lets a malicious guest push a file to a connecting technician's machine and have the technician's own client run it. No prompt appears. In one case on November 12, a pushed batch file installed a rogue ScreenConnect client pointing at the attacker's relay in about 9 seconds, Huntress researcher John Hammond said.

Between October 20 and November 16, Huntress saw at least 688,000 guest "run file" requests hitting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses.

Huntress advises updating host clients to 26.6.5 or later. If that is not possible, it recommends removing the TransferFiles permission from roles and session groups.
key_points: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets a ScreenConnect guest run a payload on a technician's PC without any prompt.
Huntress counted at least 688,000 malicious run-file requests against 42 servers between October 20 and November 16.
Fix: update ScreenConnect host clients to 26.6.5 or later, or remove the TransferFiles permission.

sources.name: Check Point Research
sources.title: Drupal patches critical flaw letting unauthenticated attackers reinstall sites

stories.headline: Drupal patches critical flaw that lets attackers reinstall sites
stories.dek: CVE-2026-132165 can let unauthenticated attackers abuse the installer to seize a site or run code; fixes are out for Drupal 10 and 11.
stories.body:
Drupal has released security updates for CVE-2026-132165, a critical vulnerability in the content management system. Under certain conditions, unauthenticated attackers could exploit the installation process to reinstall Drupal, take control of affected websites or execute arbitrary code, according to Check Point Research.

The fixed versions are Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. Site operators on those branches should update.

The Drupal fix landed in a busy week for web stack patches. Check Point's weekly threat report also lists PHP updates for seven critical flaws in PHP 8.2 through 8.5, including CVE-2026-129289, rated 9.2 on the CVSS scale, which can allow unauthenticated remote code execution under specific configurations. NGINX patched five high-severity bugs, and researchers estimate about 8.8 million services may remain exposed.
key_points: Drupal's CVE-2026-132165 lets unauthenticated attackers abuse the installer under certain conditions to take over sites or run code.
Fixed versions are Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13.
PHP and NGINX also shipped fixes for serious remote code execution flaws the same week.

option_notes: ChatGPT is OpenAI's chatbot. The states' lawsuits target SpaceX over Grok.
Gemini is Google's model. The lawsuits concern Grok, which the states say still sexualizes real photos.
Claude is Anthropic's model. The suits are aimed at SpaceX over Grok.
questions.explanation: Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue over Grok, alleging it still sexualizes real photos of women and children. They also say users as young as 13 may have been exposed via X.

questions.question: Why did The Binding of Isaac's Steam reviews crash to Overwhelmingly Negative?
options: An update added intrusive new DRM
The new DLC launched full of crashes
An update added undisclosed AI music
The base game got a steep price hike
option_notes: DRM was not the issue. Players objected to AI-generated music added without an AI disclosure.
Crashes were not the cause. The review bomb followed AI-generated music in a GTA 6-parodying update.
No price hike was involved. The backlash was over undisclosed AI-generated music.
questions.explanation: A GTA 6-parodying update added AI-generated music without disclosure, prompting a review bomb. Creator Edmund McMillen called it a "shit show" before the music was removed.

story.headline: Binding of Isaac pulls AI music after reviews crash to Overwhelmingly Negative

questions.question: Which Unreal Engine feature will Unreal Engine 6 drop, reversing Epic's June plan?
option_notes: Nanite was not named. Epic is dropping Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework.
Verse is staying. Gameplay moves to Verse and Scene Graph as Blueprints go away.
Lumen was not named. The feature leaving UE6 is Blueprints.
questions.explanation: Epic had said in June that Blueprints would coexist in UE6 but now expects AI to largely handle UE5-to-UE6 conversion. Freshly Baked Games, maker of Queen's Domain, plans to switch engines over the pivot.

story.headline: Unreal Engine 6 drops Blueprints, bets on Verse and AI

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding

questions.question: Why did OpenRouter remove three AI providers from Zero Data Retention eligibility?
options: They were caught training on user prompts
Attackers were copying prompts inside them
option_notes: Safety benchmarks were not the issue. The problem was prompt theft inside three inference hosts.
The providers were not training on data. Dragos found attackers inside the hosts copying requests.
Outages were not the reason. Attackers were silently copying requests, and the providers never noticed.
questions.explanation: Dragos canary tests covering about two million prompts found requests being copied, some marked Zero Data Retention. OpenRouter pulled three providers and 125 endpoints, though none has been named.

story.headline: OpenRouter drops three AI providers after months of prompt theft

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
